subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Hadith on Etiquette of Eating
overview: The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught a young person how to eat in a way that remembers Allah and respects the people sharing the food. In this sub-strand you will read that Hadith, practise the manners of eating, and learn the benefit of saying Bismillah.

lessons.title: The Hadith on how to eat
objectives: Read the selected Hadith on the manners of eating.
Name the three instructions in the Hadith.
Explain each instruction in simple words.
lessons.intro: A shared plate of food can become a scramble if nobody knows the manners. The Prophet (S.A.W.) once watched a young boy eating and gave him three clear instructions that Muslims still follow.
lessons.notes:
### The selected Hadith
The Prophet (S.A.W.) said: “Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right, and eat what is directly in front of you.” This Hadith is narrated by Al-Bukhari. He said it to a young person, Umar ibn Abi Salamah, whose hand was moving about in the dish.

### The three instructions
1. Mention the name of Allah. Before eating, say “Bismillah”, which means “In the name of Allah”. If you forget until you have started, say “Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah”, meaning “In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end”.
2. Eat with your right hand. The right hand is used for eating unless it is injured and cannot be used. The left hand is not the sunnah for eating when the right hand is well.
3. Eat what is directly in front of you. Take the food nearest to you. Do not reach across the plate into someone else’s share, and do not search the dish for the best piece while others are eating from the same plate.

### Reading it carefully
The three parts belong together. Saying Bismillah without grabbing food from every side is incomplete, and eating neatly without remembering Allah is also incomplete. Write the Hadith in your notebook exactly in meaning, and be able to read it aloud. These manners are sunnah: the way of the Prophet (S.A.W.). Following them at breakfast, at school and at a wedding meal is part of loving that sunnah.

keyWords.meaning: the correct and polite way of doing something
the teaching and practice of the Prophet (S.A.W.)

examples.problem: At a family meal, a boy starts eating at once with his left hand and picks meat from the far side of the plate. Which parts of the Hadith has he missed?
steps: He did not mention the name of Allah.
He used the left hand while the right hand was free.
He ate from what was not in front of him.
examples.answer: He missed all three: Bismillah, the right hand, and eating from what is in front of him.

activity.title: Read the Hadith in pairs
steps: Read the Hadith aloud together: “Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right, and eat what is directly in front of you.”
One partner asks, “What do we do before eating?” and the other answers from the Hadith. Swap and cover the other two instructions.
Write the Hadith in your notebook and underline the three instructions.
Tell the narrator: Al-Bukhari.

practice.question: State the three instructions in the Hadith of eating.
practice.answer: Mention the name of Allah, eat with your right hand, and eat what is directly in front of you.

practice.question: Who narrated this Hadith, as given in the Grade 4 design?
What do you say if you forget Bismillah until after you have started eating?

summary: The Hadith gives three manners: say Bismillah, eat with the right hand, and eat from in front of you.
The three manners go together at every meal.

lessons.title: Showing the manners of eating
objectives: Demonstrate the etiquette of eating step by step.
Add other sunnah manners that keep a meal clean and thankful.
Role-play a shared meal with correct manners.
lessons.intro: Manners of eating are easier to remember when the hands do them, not only the mouth. Washing, sitting, saying Bismillah and stopping when you are satisfied turn a meal into a sunnah.
lessons.notes:
### A simple order to follow
Use this order whenever you eat:

- Wash your hands.
- Sit down. Do not eat while walking about or reclining in a careless way.
- Say Bismillah.
- Take food with the right hand, from the part in front of you.
- Eat calmly, chew the food, and do not fill the mouth so much that you cannot speak politely.
- Do not waste. Take an amount you can finish.
- If the food is not to your taste, leave it without insulting the cook. The Prophet (S.A.W.) did not criticise food. If he liked it he ate, and if he did not he left it (Bukhari).
- When you finish, say Alhamdulillah, praise be to Allah, and wash your hands again.

### Eating with others
A shared meal needs extra care. Wait for others if that is the custom of the house. Do not reach over a person’s arm. Do not blow into a shared cup of water. Offer food to a guest or a classmate before taking more yourself. Talking is allowed, but do not talk with a full mouth, and do not make fun of what someone else is eating.

### Demonstration
Practise with a real piece of fruit or with an empty plate in class so that the actions become a habit. The aim is not a play for one day. The aim is that lunch at home looks the same as the demonstration. These manners uphold the sunnah and show respect for the blessing on the plate.

keyWords.meaning: praise be to Allah; said after eating
to throw away or spoil food that could have been eaten

examples.problem: The rice is slightly burnt. One child shouts, “This food is terrible!” What is the sunnah response?
steps: The Prophet (S.A.W.) did not criticise food.
If you can eat it, eat from your side and say Bismillah.
If you truly cannot, leave it quietly and still thank Allah for the meal.
examples.answer: Do not insult the food. Eat it if you can, or leave it without complaining, and say Alhamdulillah.

activity.title: Demonstrate and role-play a meal
materials: A basin of water and soap, or a picture of handwashing
An empty plate and a cup
A short video of good eating manners if the school has a device
steps: Watch a short clip, or watch your teacher, showing handwashing, sitting, Bismillah, the right hand and eating from the front of the plate.
Each learner demonstrates the same steps with an empty plate.
In small groups, role-play a shared lunch: include one learner who forgets Bismillah and is gently reminded.
End every role-play by saying Alhamdulillah.

practice.question: List four steps of eating etiquette in the correct order, beginning with the hands.
practice.answer: Wash the hands, sit, say Bismillah, and eat with the right hand from what is in front of you.

practice.question: What did the Prophet (S.A.W.) do if he did not like a food?
practice.answer: He left it. He did not criticise it.

practice.question: What do you say when you finish eating?
Why should you take only what you can finish?
practice.answer: So that food is not wasted. Food is a blessing from Allah.

summary: Wash, sit, say Bismillah, eat with the right hand from in front of you, and say Alhamdulillah.
Do not criticise food or waste it.
A shared plate needs extra care for the people beside you.

lessons.title: Why we say Bismillah and keep the sunnah
objectives: Explain the benefit of saying Bismillah before eating.
Show appreciation for the etiquette by choosing to follow it.
Correct a wrong eating habit using the Hadith.
lessons.intro: Saying one word before a meal can change who shares that meal. The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that mentioning Allah brings protection and blessing, and that forgetting it gives Shaytan a way in.
lessons.notes:
### The benefit of Bismillah
Bismillah remembers that the food is from Allah, not from our own power. It asks blessing, called barakah, on the meal. The Prophet (S.A.W.) taught that when a person mentions the name of Allah, Shaytan does not share that food, and that when the name is left out, Shaytan eats with the person (Muslim). So the benefit is both spiritual and practical: the heart is grateful, the meal is blessed, and an enemy of the believer is kept away.

If you forget at the first bite, you have not lost the chance. Say “Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah” as soon as you remember. Teach a younger child the same words. A family that begins together with Bismillah is following the sunnah the Prophet taught a young person like you.

### Appreciating the etiquette
Appreciation is shown by practice, not only by a high mark. A learner who knows the Hadith and still snatches food has not yet valued it. Decide on three promises:

- I will say Bismillah before I eat, at home and at school.
- I will eat with my right hand from the food in front of me.
- I will not waste food or insult it.

These promises uphold the sunnah. They also keep the table peaceful, because nobody’s hand is fighting for the same piece. Thank Allah after the meal. The food, the hand that cooked it and the rain that grew it are all reasons for Alhamdulillah.

keyWords.meaning: Satan, who whispers evil and tries to share a meal begun without Allah’s name

examples.problem: Maryam remembers Bismillah only after three mouthfuls. What should she say, and what benefit does mentioning Allah still bring?
steps: She says Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah.
Mentioning Allah keeps Shaytan from sharing the rest of the meal.
She continues with the right hand and does not waste the food.
examples.answer: She says Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah. Mentioning Allah brings barakah and protection from Shaytan sharing the food.

activity.title: Role-play the benefit of Bismillah
steps: In groups, role-play two meals: one begun without Bismillah, with pushing and waste, and one begun with Bismillah and the right hand.
After the scenes, discuss the benefit of saying Bismillah.
Each learner writes the three promises from the lesson in the notebook.
Share one promise with the class.

practice.question: State two benefits of saying Bismillah before eating.
practice.answer: It brings barakah and it keeps Shaytan from sharing the meal. It also remembers that food is from Allah.

practice.question: Which Hadith collection reports that Shaytan shares a meal when Allah’s name is not mentioned?
How does a learner show that he or she appreciates the etiquette of eating?
practice.answer: By practising it: saying Bismillah, eating with the right hand, eating from in front, and not wasting food.

summary: Bismillah brings barakah and keeps Shaytan from sharing the meal.
If you forget, say Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirah.
Appreciation means keeping these manners at every meal.

quiz.question: Which three instructions are in the Hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari?
options: Run, shout and stand
Mention Allah’s name, eat with the right, eat from in front of you
Eat in silence, eat alone, eat at night only
Use the left hand, blow on the food, waste nothing
quiz.explanation: The Hadith says: mention the name of Allah, eat with your right, and eat what is directly in front of you.

quiz.question: What does Bismillah mean?
options: Praise be to Allah
In the name of Allah
Allah is the Greatest
Peace be upon you
quiz.explanation: Bismillah is said before eating and before many other actions.

quiz.question: You forget Bismillah until you have already started. What should you say?
quiz.explanation: It means “In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.”

quiz.question: Which hand is the sunnah for eating when both hands are well?
options: Either hand
The left hand
The right hand
Both hands at once in the shared plate
quiz.explanation: The Hadith says to eat with the right.

quiz.question: Why do you eat from the food directly in front of you?
options: So that you take a friend’s share
So that you do not reach across other people
Because the middle is always haram
Because the Hadith forbids sitting
quiz.explanation: The Hadith teaches this manner for a shared meal.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet (S.A.W.) do about food he did not like?
options: He criticised the cook
He threw it away in anger
He left it without criticising it
He forced everyone to leave it
quiz.explanation: If he liked food he ate it, and if he did not he left it. He did not criticise it.

quiz.question: What is said when the meal is finished?
options: Bismillah only
Alhamdulillah
Allahu Akbar as a replacement for thanks
Nothing
quiz.explanation: Alhamdulillah thanks Allah for the food.

quiz.question: What happens when a person eats without mentioning Allah, according to the Hadith in Muslim?
options: The food becomes sweeter
Shaytan shares the meal
The food must be thrown away
Wudhu is performed on the plate
quiz.explanation: Mentioning Allah keeps Shaytan from sharing the food.

quiz.question: Which action best shows appreciation of the eating etiquette?
options: Knowing the Hadith and still wasting food
Saying Bismillah and eating with the right hand every day
Eating while walking because it is faster
Insulting food that is plain
quiz.explanation: Appreciation is shown by following the sunnah at real meals.

quiz.question: Barakah in a meal means…
quiz.explanation: Saying Bismillah is a way of asking for that blessing.

sources: KICD Grade 4 Islamic Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 2.0 Hadith, Sub-strand 2.2 Hadith on Etiquette of Eating
Sahih al-Bukhari: Hadith to Umar ibn Abi Salamah on mentioning Allah, the right hand and eating from what is in front
Sahih Muslim: Hadith on Shaytan sharing a meal when Allah’s name is not mentioned; Sahih al-Bukhari: the Prophet did not criticise food
